a found or absent motif each moves the strategy."},{"criterion":"open","value":5,"reason":"Names model runs (capsid × receptor × pose); measurements stop at single-digit modeled complexes, far within $1,000 of H100-hours."},{"criterion":"reshape","value":1,"reason":"Sequential says none: every pair is an independent job, only embarrassingly parallel copies fill the hardware."}]},{"id":"Option 2: Microsecond molecular dynamics of capsid–receptor–membrane assemblies","distance":"ADJACENT","distance_reason":"Same subject — capsid–receptor binding physics — but asks whether pH-release and membrane effects are visible, not which variants transcytose or which signatures.","scores":[{"criterion":"stakes","value":3,"reason":"Answer would refine whether binding-step physics yields a trafficking signature; no concrete buy/build choice clearly turns on it yet."},{"criterion":"open","value":1,"reason":"Calls the compute question settled: published work already states longer trajectories are needed and known to reveal more configurational space."},{"criterion":"reshape","value":3,"reason":"Names ~5×10^8 serial steps, replica parallelism, and an MSM restructure gated on metastability, but one run fills a GPU."}]},{"id":"Option 3: Supervised sequence-to-transcytosis phenotype models","distance":"SAME","distance_reason":"Its object is transcytosis phenotype per variant — literally the root's 'which variants transcytose' sub-question, approached statistically.","scores":[{"criterion":"stakes","value":5,"reason":"Whether to scale labeled transcytosis data or model compute, and which variants to validate next, turns directly on the answer."},{"criterion":"open","value":5,"reason":"Names seeds, architectures, model size; measurements stop at ~240K-variant libraries and six-model ensembles, within $1,000 reach."},{"criterion":"reshape","value":3,"reason":"Names gradient-update chain and seed/trait-model parallelism, but a cited source already trains these AAV models that way and one run fills a GPU."}]},{"id":"Option 4: Cryo-EM reconstruction of capsid–receptor complexes","distance":"SAME","distance_reason":"Interface mapping of which capsid residues contact which receptor domains is a sub-question feeding the root's binding-signature question.","scores":[{"criterion":"stakes","value":3,"reason":"Structures would refine interface knowledge, but which complexes to solve next is incremental and no singular buy/build choice hinges on the answer."},{"criterion":"open","value":1,"reason":"Calls the compute question settled: published atlas already shows resolution improves with particle count, covering the reachable effect."},{"criterion":"reshape","value":3,"reason":"Names a dozen sequential stages and per-particle parallelism, but a cited AAV system already runs this chain in parallel on GPUs."}]},{"id":"Option 5: Cross-species receptor–capsid compatibility scoring","distance":"SAME","distance_reason":"Asks whether binding signatures learned in mouse survive in humans — a sub-question of the root's which-signatures question.","scores":[{"criterion":"stakes","value":4,"reason":"Determines which conserved receptor signatures and capsid candidates advance toward human use; a real collect/scale choice moves either way."},{"criterion":"open","value":5,"reason":"Names model runs over ortholog × capsid pairs; measurements stop at a handful of isoforms for one capsid, well within reach."},{"criterion":"reshape","value":1,"reason":"Sequential says none: each ortholog–capsid pair is an independent modeling job, only a sweep of copies fills hardware."}]}]}
